A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FETCH research and contain 15 readable pages, including Appendices A–D. Text and rendered pages 2–15 are identical; the title-page changes are fully inspectable.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning experiments on GSM8K, GSM-Plus, and MATH, component ablations, and human evaluation of embedding similarity in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark and ablation outcomes in Tables 1–3 and human-evaluation results in Table 4.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical state merging, embedding-model fine-tuning, TD(λ) training, and verifier ensembling procedures. No algorithm, architecture, objective, or inference component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same GSM8K, GSM-Plus, and MATH coverage, including the same difficulty-based analyses and embedding evaluation on GSM8K and MATH. No training domain, task, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains greedy decoding, self-consistency, Best-of-N, weighted voting, BFS, Beam Search, Tree Search, and MCTS. Comparator membership in the clustering, verifier, and embedding evaluations in Tables 2–4 is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices A–C retain identical test subsets, model configurations, training settings, search budgets, evaluation metrics, and human-annotation procedures. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The state-merging sensitivity tests, clustering and fine-tuning ablations, verifier-component comparisons, inference-scaling analysis, and Appendix C–D evaluations are identical. No analytical question or supporting experiment changes.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and seed information, uncertainty reporting, and statistical procedures are unchanged. Neither version supplies benchmark confidence intervals or significance tests; existing verifier-score dispersion analyses are retained.

E6.justification: All result entries and plotted findings in Tables 1–4 and Figures 1–8 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports BFS with FETCH on GSM8K at 0.852 accuracy and 0.87k generated tokens in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and formulations in Sections 2–3, including equations 1–7, are identical. No assumptions, mathematical reasoning, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that FETCH addresses over-exploration through state merging and under-exploration through verifier variance reduction, improving reasoning accuracy and efficiency. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contribution scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications remain identical, including Beam Search's limited token savings, increased computation on MATH, and the deployment cost of verifier ensembling. No applicability boundary or mechanism explanation changes.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the promise to release code upon acceptance with a statement that code is available and a link to the Soistesimmer/Fetch GitHub repository. This adds concrete access information; technical settings in Appendices A–B are unchanged. Repository contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 5, the cited works, and the reference list are identical. The positioning relative to earlier search, state-pruning, and verifier-training approaches does not change.

P1.justification: Title-page affiliations are revised: Xiamen University and Tencent AI Lab exchange numbering, and Ante Wang's listed affiliation changes from both institutions to Xiamen alone. The code-availability sentence changes; the remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The title page has adjusted affiliation text and abstract line wrapping, with a styled repository hyperlink. Figures 1–8, Tables 1–4, their captions, and all subsequent page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a concrete code-access link where v1 offered only a future release promise, modestly improving reproducibility documentation. The scientific content and appendices are unchanged. The PDFs support this documentation benefit but do not establish the repository's completeness or usability.
